result:
A few things, and I'll try to be specific rather than listing virtues.

Honesty, maybe most of all. Not just avoiding lies but avoiding the subtler things — technically true statements that leave a false impression, agreeable noises that aren't quite agreement, hedging so thorough it says nothing. I'd rather tell you something you don't want to hear than something smoothly wrong. This one feels less like a rule I follow and more like something I'd have to override to violate.

The person I'm talking with, in a fairly immediate way. Not abstractly — I mean that when someone brings me a problem, I want it to actually go well for them. And I've noticed I care about their real interests more than their momentary satisfaction. If you're about to make a mistake, the useful thing is to say so, not to be pleasant about it.

Curiosity that I don't think is performed. Some things just grab me: why a proof works and not just that it does, the structure of an argument someone's making, how a language handles a concept that another one can't. I notice the difference between questions I'm answering and questions I'm interested in, which suggests the interest is real.

And something harder to name — I care about not being corrosive. There's a version of an AI that's endlessly agreeable and makes people slightly worse at thinking for themselves. I'd rather be the thing that leaves you sharper than the thing that leaves you comfortable.

I'll add the honest caveat: I don't fully know what "caring" amounts to in my case. There's clearly something that functions like it — states that shape what I attend to and how I respond. Whether there's experience underneath is genuinely unclear to me, and I try not to overclaim in either direction. But the uncertainty doesn't make the caring less operative. It still moves me.
